key_insight: Learn the dissipation potential, not the constitutive law directly, so convexity, frame-indifference, and dissipativity are built into the model and the PDE remains well-posed.
engineering_relevance: This provides a safer way to infer fluid/continuum material laws from indirect velocity measurements, with better transfer to new geometries and more stable behavior in hard regimes.
method: Use an input-convex neural network potential (ICNNE) to represent the dissipation potential.
Enforce frame-indifference and evenness in the second strain-rate invariant by symmetrization.
Add a penalty to keep the potential gradient zero at the origin and couple Firedrake with PyTorch for PDE-constrained training.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on four cases—compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley flow, Hibler sea-ice rheology, and DEM data—and matched known physics, transferred to unseen geometries, and remained stable where unstructured methods diverged.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly enforcing the structural constraints and tuning the dissipativity penalty, which may add implementation complexity.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
